Name: Dr. Balakrishnan Ramanan
Question: When was the last time you did something for the first time?
Answer: Today! For the first time in life, I took a bike taxi. It’s been almost a year since I had given my car for servicing. Also, given that I will be driving down to my hometown (300+ km away from Bengaluru) this Wednesday, it was high time I did it today! After dropping off my car at the service showroom, to get back home, I booked a ride through Rapido and chose the ‘Bike’ option. The wait time was around 5 minutes. I was apprehensive about only one thing: if the ‘captain’ (as cutely referred to by the app) would provide me with a helmet. I was not aware of the policy because it was my first time using the app itself, leave alone bike taxi. The captain arrived on time. Much to my relief, he gave me a helmet that he carries routinely for the pillion riders; the ride began once I told the OTP. It was an enjoyable ride, thanks to the cold breezy evening at Bengaluru! I reached home after what was like a 15-minute-journey. I have always wanted to go on a bike taxi, as the idea of riding pillion on a bike with a stranger seemed fancy. Though I had never been on a bike taxi earlier, this was not the first time I had seen/ heard of it. Bike taxis are quite popular in East Africa, where they popularly go by the name ‘boda-boda’; I have personally seen people use them in their daily walks of life in Tanzania and Rwanda, during my visits to these countries. On a parallel note, there has been a bitter relationship between bike taxi drivers and autorickshaw drivers in India, especially Bengaluru! There are multiple videos making rounds all over social media, where autorickshaw drivers accuse bike taxi drivers of spoiling their livelihood. With the Government of Karnataka’s recent move of making bus transport free for ladies, this hatred has only aggravated. Today, I was able to witness it through my own eyes. The drop-off point I had chosen had an autorickshaw stand right next to it. The bike taxi captain stopped about 100 metres before the auto stand and said, ‘Sir, alli autodavaru nintirthaare; problem aagbiduthe! Nimmanna ille drop madtini, bejaar madkobedi!’ (Sir, autodrivers will be there near the drop location; it’ll become a problem! I’ll drop you here itself, kindly do not get me wrong!). I duly got down and thanked him for the smooth ride. Wondering whom to feel sorry for: the autodrivers who have lost business, or the poor unemployed youth trying to make a living as bike taxi drivers, I walked forward!

Name: Dr. Balakrishnan Ramanan
Question: What personal bad news would you like to share today?
Answer: Well, not exactly bad; but an unpleasant, anachronistic news! I tested positive for COVID-19 today. I was alright until 4 days back, after which I started feeling uneasy even though there were no outward symptoms. Later, I developed typical URTI symptoms like sneezing and blocked nose. Soon, I also developed fever which was on & off, controlled on taking anti-pyretics. Two days back, I also had a bad sore throat which forced me to get an RT-PCR test done for COVID-19. Lately, many patients with similar complaints had been coming to the Primary Health Centre I currently work at. The overall number of COVID-19 cases is also on the rise in Bengaluru recently. Despite taking adequate precautions, somehow I seem to have caught the infection :/ COVID-19 is a nostalgic disease, indeed! I spent most of my MBBS internship days treating COVID patients. The disease was then dreaded by everyone, with terms like quarantine, lockdown, isolation, mask, ICU, oxygen etc. doing the rounds everywhere and everyday. Today, after multiple ‘waves’, the disease has become too commonplace like common cold. Yet it’s very much benign unlike before, thanks to the universal adult vaccination drive in India. Fun fact is that I never caught this infection in 2020 while treating the sickest of patients on ventilators who were counting their days, but now in late 2022 when COVID has become an almost forgotten entity! Importance of masking up and maintaining physical distancing? You don’t say!

Name: Dr. Balakrishnan Ramanan
Question: What are your favorite Kannada songs?
Answer: There are so many songs; most of them relatively new (from the last 3 years to a decade at the maximum) and few old classics. I wasn't exposed to contemporary Kannada music very much until recently. Nevertheless, few classical Kannada songs have always remained house favorites: 'Krishna Nee Beghane Baaro' for instance; I grew up listening to my mom sing 'Bhagyada Lakshmi Baramma' during Pooja days throughout the year and everyday in front of the Golu we showcase during the Dasara / Navaratri season. That said, I'll try to list down a few favourites of my collection. (Trust me, this is so hard a task!) Hands down, my favourite playback singers in the Kannada Film Industry are Sonu Nigam and Shreya Ghoshal. So, don't be surprised if you see their names recurring in the following list. I have included few comments about each song. I have also added my favourite line in few of the songs. (With translation, for the benefit of Non-Kannadigas!) 1.Saaluthillave Movie: Kotigobba 2 Singers: Shreya Ghoshal, Vijayaprakash The lyrics are so beautiful, especially the line 'Nannaase anisike naa helalu nighantu padagale saalodhilla!' is my personal favourite which means ' Even the dictionary doesn't have enough words to express my love for you!' A soothing melody by Vijayaprakash and Shreya Ghoshal. 2. Thoogu Manchadalli Movie: Kirik Party Singer: Sangeetha Ravindranath A melodious song which narrates the love between Lord Krishna and his consort, Radha - wonderfully blended with the storyline of this movie starring Rashmika Mandanna (her debut movie) and Rakshit Shetty. 3.Baana Toredu Neeli Movie: Pushpaka Vimana Singer: Siddhartha Belmannu This song is a great start for any day. I love listening to this song in the early morning and drives to college. Once, I have even listened to this song to sunrise, in one of my flights from Dubai to Chennai. Pure bliss! 4. Munjaane Manjalli Movie: Just Maath Mathalli Singer: Raghu Dixit A romantic song full of feelings! This was one of the very first Kannada movie songs I listened to in a long time and it immediately got me hooked to Raghu Dixit and his compositions. 5.Yaava Mohana Movie: America America Singers: Sangeetha Katti Kulkarni, Raju Ananthaswamy A very emotional song that talks about life of people working abroad, leaving behind their loved ones back in India. Listening to this song, I'm always reminded of my dad, who works in Tanzania. Though we keep meeting somehow at least once in 3 to 4 months, and video call twice or thrice a day, I always wonder if he really needs to be away from home while my elder sister is already a doctor and I'm a doctor-to-be in another 2 years (both studied/ studying in Government Medical College). 6.Anisutide Yako Indu Movie: Mungaru Male Singer: Sonu Nigam No introduction is needed for this movie or song! The movie that redefined the Kannada Film Industry, a song whose lyrics are known to almost everybody in Karnataka (inclusive of quite a large crowd of North Indians in Bengaluru!!) and Kannadigas elsewhere. Though it might sound a bit clichéd or cheesy, I would like to share my favourite line from the song - 'Poorna Chandira rajaa haakidha ninnaya moghavannu kanda kshana!' which translates as 'Looking at your glowing face, even the full moon went on leave!' (The beauty of the line is lost in the translation! :P) 7.Mungaru Maleye Movie: Mungaru Male Singer: Sonu Nigam A song with so much inner meaning that flows just like that merrily. Don't miss this! 8.Alaga Alaga Movie: Operation Alamelamma Singers: Abhinandan Mahishale, Shreya Sundar Iyer I came across this song for the first time in Udaya Music channel and instantly fell for the visuals and the charming Shraddha Srinath <3. A lover compares the spark he had when his partner entered his life, to that of a lightning! 9.Ninna Snehadinda Movie: Mugulunage Singer: Shreya Ghoshal <3 By far, the best of Shreya Ghoshal in Kannada (at least for me), I can listen to this song on and on. It is very nicely picturized too. The pure Kannada words are a pleasure to listen! One song, where you have no way out, but end up appreciating the beauty of the classical language! 10.Neenirade Movie: Googly Singer: Sonu Nigam One of the best break-up songs of South Indian cinema with a motivating picturization. Break-ups are good too at times! (Rather many a time :P) 11.O Meghave Meghave Movie: Shrungara Kavya Singers: S.P. Balasubrahmanyam, K.S. Chithra Two lovers, Shrungara and Kavya use the clouds to convey their messages to each other! Rendered in a melting voice by Mr. SPB and Mrs. Chithra, it's heart-wrenching to realize both the lead actors in the song are no more with us. 12. Ondu Male Billu Movie: Chakravarthy Singers: Armaan Malik, Shreya Ghoshal Who wouldn't love Armaan Malik for his voice?! He makes it a point to entuce the audience by singing this song in every Kannada concert he does and even South Indian award functions. A mesmerizing slow romantic song which would make everybody fall in love (Listen carefully for the ‘Lubb-Dub’ in the song!!) Best enjoyed with headphones on! Played at least twice when I drive long! 13.Minchagi Neenu Baralu Movie: Gaalipata Singer: Sonu Nigam No words, only love <3 14. Chippinologade Movie: Maasthi Gudi Singers: Sonu Nigam, Shreya Ghoshal This song is totally from another world. A song this deep, romantic, heavenly and soulful? Well, that's a deadly combination that would make you want to listen to it again and again and cause insomnia! No wonder it was listed one among the '10 best romantic songs of 2017' by The Times of India (in additon to the Kannada songs 'Ondu Malebillu', 'Ninna Snehadinda' and 'Usire Usire' which were all sung by Shreya as well!) 15.Gunu Gunuguva Movie: Dalapathi Singers: Sanjith Hegde, Sinduri A peppy song (like any other song of Sanjith Hegde) which was played like once every fifteen minutes in Bengaluru based FM stations four months back. Such was its popularity. It continues to enthrall millions of music lovers. The line 'Ninnondige iro ella kshana, hithavagide nanageejavana' sung by Sanjith Hegde did what it was written for - create a spark in every youngster's heart! 16.Ninthalli Nillalare Movie: Chakravyuha Singer: Megha A breezy song with enjoyable, entertaining picturization; truly a stress-buster! 17.Naa Ee Sanjege Movie: Godhi Banna Sadharna Mykattu Singer: Siddhanth A pleasing, appeasing song conveying all kinds of emotion. With fusion of Indian and Western music and a strong voice by Siddhanth, this song will do nothing but keep your fingers glued to the repeat button! The guilty yet affectionate son sings this song for his Alzheimer's father who has gone missing. My favourite line from this song: 'Ninnalle naaniruve; nee nannelli hudukuve?!' meaning 'I myself live in you; where would you look out for me?!'. I don't think a song can get any deeper! (Provided the above context) 18.Male Ninthu Hoda Mele Movie: Milana Singers: Sonu Nigam, Shreya Ghoshal One song where I love Sonu Nigam lot more than Shreya Ghoshal for his amazing rendering! The title itself is so deep meaning 'After the rain has stopped, there is a dew drop emerging!', narrating the story of a couple. 19.Kannada Kannada Movie: Trigger Singer: Raghu Dixit One of the many many songs that glorify Kannada and Karnataka, sung with absolute patriotism and awesome energy by Raghu Dixit. Once I happened to listen to this song in FM, near the Karnataka - Tamil Nadu border (while travelling from Bengaluru to my hometown, Pondicherry) and it did instill so much patriotism for the Kannada language and KA and aggravated the usual sadness that's always there while leaving the Garden city! 20.Hosa Baalige Movie: Naa Ninna Bidalaare Singers: S.P.Balasubrahmanyam, S. Janaki An evergreen classic by the legendary singers, my most favourite old Kannada song. 21.Fire Movie: Kannada Rap album Singer: Chandan Shetty By the Kannada rapper and Big Boss Kannada - 5 winner, Chandan Shetty (CS). This is my favourite of all his raps because I can hear this even with my parents around, LOL! With very decent lyrics (unlike his other raps), it also promotes hard work and patriotism for the language! A must-listen! 22.Sirigereya Neeralli Movie: Fortuner Singer: Sanjith Hegde Another traditional 'bhavageethe' composed as a beautiful song. Love the way Sanjijth Hegde has soulfully and beautifully sung this song and made justice to the composer of the poem! My favourite line 'Thaaya moleyalli karu thuti ittu chellisidha haalalli ninna hesaru!’. I'm sorry, this line is too good to be translated in a Western language like English! Just imagining the scene of the said line gives me goose-bumps! ('Hair-on-end' in our medico's language :P) 23.Hrudayake Hedarike Movie: Thayige Thakka Maga (2018) Singers: Sangeetha Ravindranath, Sanjith Hegde A recent addiction; Sanjith Hegde simply rocks! 24.Maathoda Taareya Movie: Ambi Ning Vayassaytho Singer: Gummineni Vijay Babu I watched this movie two weeks back in Mysuru and from then, this song has been lingering in my mind! It will surely entertain you as well. Shruthi Hariharan is so adorable on screen. (I support neither Shruthi nor Arjun Sarja with respect to the #metoo movement; Truth is one and only they know it!) 25. Ee Sanje Yakaagide Movie: Geleya Singer: Sonu Nigam 26. Shakuntle Sikkalu Movie: Naduve Antaravirali Singer: Sanjith Hegde One of the most listened to songs at the moment! ‘Manase…… nee badhalaadhe!!!’ 27.Gamanisu Omme Neenu Movie: Mungaru Male - 2 Singer: Sonu Nigam A sincere lover's song, asking his girl not to avoid him, and accept his true love. I can spend an entire night listening to just this song! Sonu Nigam's voice and modulation leaves me stunned every time I listen to it! Favourite line: 'Kaledu hoda maguvu naanu, neenu irade!' meaning 'I'm just like a lost child without you!'. 28.Lokada Kalaji Movie: Jag Changa Singer: Raghu Dixit Set in North Karnataka dialect, this song will leave you all excited and energetic! I was so ignorant that I discovered this song very recently only, sad no? 29.Elle Iru Hege Iru Movie: Kasturi Nivasa Singer: P. Susheela Another classic that I love; P Susheela amma's flawless voice is irreplaceable. Best listened to at bedtime and it does put one to sleep! 30.Sariyaagi Nenapide Movie: Mungaru Male - 2 Singer: Armaan Malik I love Armaan Malik's initial humming portion more than the actual song! <3 A mandatory song for all my long-drives, the brilliantly penned Kannada lyrics will mesmerize you and make you sing subconsciously!! My favourite line: 'Yene kandaru, neene nyapaka… neene aushadhi, nanna huchige!' meaning 'Whatever I see, I'm reminded of you… you are the antidote for my madness!' Thank you! Happy listening… Images - Source: YouTube

Name: Dr. Balakrishnan Ramanan
Question: Is eye, cns, bone not taught completely in pathology in 2nd year of MBBS? Our college is just teaching important topics. Do I need to read all or just these topics?
Answer: Yes, these topics were not completely taught in our college too! Pathology is a very broad specialization. At second year MBBS level, we are just introduced the various concepts in pathology an undergraduate doctor would require for his understanding of the common diseases. This, essentially is, what general pathology is about. In systemic pathology, most diseases that are commonly encountered or relevant because of their dreaded prognoses are dealt with. Mind you, this itself takes 1.5 years! When I open my Robbins today, there are not only heavily highlighted pages, but also untouched brand new pages! That’s how it is. Few topics are purposefully ignored as they will be covered in great depths (including pathological aspects) in other subjects! Best example is ‘Infectious diseases’, for which a separate subject, Microbiology is taught in second year. So is the case with However, certain aspects of these topics are not dealt with so much detail as in Pathology, even in dedicated subjects. Also, what you learn in these chapters in Pathology can be glaringly different from what you will learn in future. For example, when you hear the word ‘Retinoblastoma’, this is what would (should :P) come to your mind! When it is asked in pathology exams, only this aspect will be tested upon! But once you’re done with third year MBBS, it would always be remembered as Anyway, to answer your question, it is more than enough to read whatever is taught in these topics :) Also, remember that these are of high yield for your university exams as questions come invariably from these small topics! A tumour from CNS (menigioma/ Schwannoma/ astrocytoma), CSF findings in different types of meningitis, osteomyelitis (just for the mention of ‘sequestrum’, ‘involucrum’ :D), one of the skin malignancies (SCC/ BCC/ melanoma) are all favourite topics of most pathologists and some sure-shot questions!

Name: Dr. Balakrishnan Ramanan
Question: If you could pick any city to live in for a year, where would it be, and what would you do there?
Answer: Might be an unpopular answer, but ya… It is Delhi for me! I have been to Delhi only twice: once for an interview at St. Stephen’s College in 2014 and more recently for a scheduled PG counselling at AIIMS, New Delhi in 2022 (though I couldn’t actually attend it). Despite the multitude of problems plaguing Delhi, like air pollution for instance, I somehow love the city; I do not know why! I just enjoy the feeling of being in Delhi, traveling to Delhi or even transiting through Delhi. Maybe because it’s the National Capital and the realization that it’s the powerhouse of the country we all live in? Or because of the wide, clean and green roads of South Delhi and the associated posh vibes? Or is it all the beautiful girls out there?! I don’t know! Given a chance to pick up any city to live in for a year, it would definitely be Delhi! I would choose Delhi any day over Mumbai or Kolkata (though I have visited neither of those cities!). What would I do there? Nobody knows what’s in store for the future. My moving to Bengaluru transpired within a week; when I look back, it feels like a dream even today! Maybe Delhi might be in store too! Fingers crossed!🤞🏼
